chapter: Return to Basie and leaving in 1948
title: Meeting Hinton and Cab Calloway at the Omaha Orpheum, February 1946
summary: Fresh from the Army, Jones sat in with Cab Calloway's band in Omaha, replacing Shadow Wilson briefly and impressing Cab with Oliver Buford.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: This is most interesting, Jo. Might I ask you, when I met you again... it was in Omaha, Nebraska. What was the name of that theatre in Omaha?
Orpheum Theatre. This was what year, because you had just gotten -
February 1946. You'd just gotten out of the Army, or had you gotten out or were you on furlough?
And Cab Calloway was playing the Orpheum Theatre?
That's right, with the Peters Sisters and you had my little favorite drummer with you, Buford.

Well Jo, here we are and another day has passed. Now this is Wednesday, January 24th and we're going to continue on talking about Kansas City, after you got out of the Army and came back to Kansas City and you ran into Cab Calloway's band with me hanging around there and we were so glad to see each other again. We finally persuaded you to sit in with us and give us a real treat.

In Omaha, you know... February of '46, of course. I got out the first of February and I did 'The King' with Basie and Preston Love, who had replaced Earl Warren during the time - he and I both went to the Pennsylvania Station, got on a train, and went right straight to Omaha. Earl sat back in the band. I said, "You got it, Shad, I'll be back later."
Oh, Shadow Wilson was in the band?

Sure he was while I was in the Army. The greatest natural drummer that ever lived. I said, "I'll be back in a minute." I think it took me about 6 weeks to get back because I had a lot of debriefing to do. Then when I came out to visit you with Fess and Cab with the Peters Sisters and all that and my little Buford Oliver was there - Fess said, "What can you do for him?" I said, "He has a long way to go but he's a young man. I'll do the best I can." So I said, "You wait," and I got in a taxi and I went and got my shoes. You know with these bad feet I always

have these special shoes to play in. So I played the show and Fess went and sat out in the audience at the Hoffman Theatre, and told him, "Now that's the way it goes." I said, "Yes but I'm not going to be with you eventually. I'm going back with Basie." But it was a wonderful thing. At that particular time Dannie Barker was contemplating writing -
